title: S. Korean Program Rewards People for Exercise
paragraphs: In South Korea, people can now earn money just by exercising. A government program called "Teunteun Money," which roughly means "sturdy money," gives people rewards for staying active, and it has become very popular.

The program is run by South Korea's Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, and it is now in its fourth year. Under the program, people record 30-minute exercise sessions and earn points. Each person can earn up to 50,000 points a year.

The points can be used like money. People can exchange them for vouchers to buy sports equipment, pay for gym memberships or shop at local stores. Recently, the points became usable at even more stores. There are now about 80,000 places across the country where people can use them.

The number of people taking part has increased quickly. By the end of July 2026, nearly 700,000 people had earned points. This was more than double the number of people at the same time the year before, which was about 317,000. On average, participants also exercised for about two more hours than a year earlier.

Because the program was so popular, the government doubled its budget to 8 billion won, or about $5.8 million. However, all of the money has already been given out. The amount of points people get for each session was also cut in half to manage the demand.

The program has also become easier to use. A special smartphone app was launched in March. In June, it started working with private fitness apps, so people can now earn points for activities such as climbing stairs and hiking.
Kim Dae-hyun, a vice minister at the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, said the program shows that exercise is becoming a part of everyday life in South Korea.
